study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective cohort with a nested randomized controlled trial.
exposure: Placental lesions (maternal vascular malperfusion, fetal vascular malperfusion, chronic inflammation)
Doppler ultrasound findings (umbilicocerebral ratio>0.8 or umbilical artery pulsatility index>p90)
Biomarkers (placental growth factor, soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1:placental growth factor ratio)
Clinical markers (fetal growth restriction, potential fetal growth restriction, small for gestational age not otherwise specified)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 294 late preterm small for gestational age pregnancies from the DRIGITAT study for whom placental pathology was available.
finding: Clinical features of fetal growth restriction in small for gestational age infants are associated with high-grade maternal vascular malperfusion and high-grade fetal vascular malperfusion, which may manifest antenatally with Doppler abnormalities.
mod_finding: Prelabor caesarean for suspected fetal distress was significantly more frequent in the group with placental pathology available (37.2%) compared to the group without (11.4%).
birth_weight: Small for gestational age (birthweight below the 10th percentile for gestational age)
gest_age: Late preterm (34 0/7 to 36 6/7 weeks) and near term
